summary: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships are funded by the UK Government (FCDO) for people from low and middle-income Commonwealth countries, including Nigeria. They pay a one-year taught master's in the UK: tuition, return airfare, a stipend of £1,712 a month (£2,000 in London) and a study travel grant. Winners have strong grades and a clear plan to use the degree for their country's development.
lookfor: Academic merit: at least a 2:1 (Second Class Upper), transcripts and references
Quality of the study plan: what you want to learn and how it links to your goals
Development impact: the problem at home, how you will apply new skills, expected change and how you will measure it
Leadership, voluntary work and a believable career plan after return
Financial need — you could not study in the UK without the award
cycle: 2027/28: CSC Central closes 20 October 2026 at 16:00 UK time (16:00 in Nigeria). Nigeria's Federal Scholarship Board advert also gives 20 October 2026. FSB shortlists and interviews, nominations go to the CSC in December 2026, results by email around July 2027, study starts September/October 2027. If you start today you have about two weeks — do the steps in order. Otherwise the next round usually opens in September.

eligibility.q: Are you a citizen (or refugee) and permanent resident of an eligible Commonwealth country such as Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya or Uganda?
eligibility.no: Look at Chevening (most countries) or university scholarships instead.

eligibility.q: Do you have, or will you have by September 2027, a first degree of at least 2:1 (Second Class Upper)?
eligibility.no: With a 2:2 the Master's award is closed to you. Consider Chevening (no degree-class rule) or the Commonwealth PhD later if you add a relevant master's.

eligibility.q: Could you afford UK study without this scholarship?
eligibility.no: If yes, you are not eligible — the CSC requires financial need.

eligibility.q: Nigeria only: do you have your NYSC certificate or exemption letter?
eligibility.no: The Federal Scholarship Board asks for NYSC evidence. Complete NYSC first, then apply in a later round.

eligibility.q: Are you free of UK government, British Council, ACU or CSC employment (and not related to a Commissioner)?
eligibility.no: You are not eligible; consider other awards.

eligibility.q: Is your chosen course a full-time one-year taught master's (not an MBA) at a UK university?
eligibility.no: Change your course choice. The CSC does not fund MBAs or part-time study.

steps.title: Confirm eligibility and your nominating body
steps.why: You cannot apply to the CSC directly. You must be nominated, and you must meet both the nominator's rules and the CSC's.
do: Open the Commonwealth Master's page and read the eligibility list.
Open the national nominating agencies list and find your country's body (Nigeria: Federal Scholarship Board, Federal Ministry of Education).
Read your nominator's advert for extra rules. Nigeria's 2027/28 advert asks for a 2:1, NYSC evidence, birth certificate, transcripts and UK admission letters.
Write down both deadlines; use the earlier one.
tips: Some NGOs are also nominators — check the NGO list if you work in one of their fields.
avoid: Thinking the CSC deadline is the only deadline — some nominators close earlier.
check: I know my nominating body and its deadline.
I meet both sets of rules.

steps.title: Understand how you will be scored
steps.why: Applications are judged on merit, the study plan and development impact. Every answer should feed one of these.
do: Open the selection criteria page.
Write the three criteria at the top of your draft document.
Pick the development problem in your country that your master's will help solve. Write it in one sentence.
Check which of the CSC development themes listed in the template form it fits, and note it.
tips: Development impact is the heart of this award — a vague 'I want to help my country' scores low.
avoid: Picking a course and then inventing a development reason for it.
check: I can state my development problem and course link in two sentences.

steps.title: Choose three UK universities and courses
steps.why: You list three course preferences in order. The CSC will not change them after selection.
do: Use the CSC's UK university list and course pages to shortlist courses.
Choose three one-year taught master's courses that all serve your development goal.
For each, note named modules, entry requirements, English requirement and application deadline.
Rank them in order of preference.
tips: Prefer courses with a dissertation or project you can base on a problem at home.
avoid: Choosing an MBA or a two-year course — not funded.
check: I have three ranked courses with reasons.

steps.title: Apply to the universities now
steps.why: The CSC does not require an offer, but Nigeria's FSB advert asks for admission from at least two UK institutions, and offers strengthen your study plan.
do: Open each university's application portal and apply.
Upload transcripts, CV, personal statement and references.
Ask for an English medium-of-instruction letter if you have no IELTS.
Upload any offer letters you already have to your CSC application.
tips: If an offer has not arrived by the deadline, keep the application receipt and ask your nominator how to submit it later.
avoid: Waiting until you win to apply for admission.
check: At least two university applications are submitted.

steps.title: Create your CSC Central account and read the template
steps.why: The template form shows every question so you can draft offline before the portal.
do: Download the 2027 Master's template form and the guidance document.
Register on CSC Central and set up two-factor authentication.
Choose your nominating body in the application.
Copy each question into a working document and draft there.
tips: Save often; the CSC warns that unsaved work can be lost.
avoid: Typing long answers straight into the portal.
check: My account works and my nominator is selected.

steps.title: Get transcripts, ID and Nigeria-specific documents
steps.why: Missing documents or missing transcript pages make the application ineligible.
do: Passport or national ID: scan the photo page as a PDF.
Transcripts: get full transcripts for every degree from your university's registry or transcript portal (budget the naira fee). Certified English translation if not in English.
Nigeria: scan your NYSC certificate, birth certificate (or declaration of age) and a passport photograph for the FSB.
Scan any UK admission letters.
Name files clearly and keep each under the upload size limit.
tips: If the official transcript will not come in time, upload your university-issued statement of result and ask your nominator about sending the official copy later.
avoid: Uploading transcripts with pages missing — this alone makes you ineligible.
check: Every document is a clear, complete PDF.

steps.title: Write the development impact statement
steps.why: This is one of the three selection criteria and the most distinctive part of the form.
do: Part 1 – the issue: describe the problem at global, national and local level, with one or two statistics, and link it to a CSC theme.
Part 2 – new skills: say what you will learn and exactly where you will apply it after return.
Part 3 – expected change: state outcomes, a timeframe and who benefits.
Part 4 – measurement: name indicators that would show the change happened (e.g. 'yield per hectare in 3 LGAs').
Cut each part to its limit.
tips: Name your employer or the organisation you will work with on return.
Small, measurable change beats grand promises.
avoid: Repeating the same sentences in all four parts.
check: Each part answers its own question and fits its limit.

steps.prompt: Four parts: the development issue; how you will apply new skills; expected outcomes, timeframe and beneficiaries; how you will measure them.
steps.limit: Separate word limits per part (reported as 200 / 100 / 250 / 100 words for 2027) — confirm in the template.

steps.title: Write your study plan
steps.why: The study plan is scored on what you want to learn and how it relates to your objectives.
do: Summarise your chosen course in two or three sentences.
Explain which modules and dissertation topic you will take and why.
Link each to a skill your development plan needs.
Mention any contact you have had with the university or offer you hold.
tips: Plan a dissertation topic based on a real problem in your country.
check: A reader can see exactly what I will learn and why.
steps.prompt: Outline and detail your proposed study in the UK and how it meets your objectives.
steps.limit: Several short fields (reported as about 525 words in total for 2027) — confirm in the form.

steps.title: Write career plans, personal statement and leadership summary
steps.why: These show you will return and use the degree, and that you already contribute beyond your job.
do: Career plans: write what you will do during the award, five years after it, and in the long term — each with concrete roles and targets.
Personal statement: explain your background and motivation and how you will contribute to development.
Voluntary and leadership activities: list specific roles with dates, what you did and results.
Check all answers tell one consistent story.
tips: Include community work, NYSC CDS projects, church/mosque or youth leadership if they show impact.
avoid: Contradictions between your career plan and development impact answers.
check: My plans are consistent across every section.
steps.prompt: Personal background and motivation; career plans (during award, 5 years, long term); voluntary and leadership activities.
steps.limit: Check the form (reported as about 500 words each for personal statement and leadership summary, 250 per career-plan field).

steps.title: Get two signed references and upload them yourself
steps.why: Unlike many awards, you upload the references. No references by the deadline means ineligible.
do: Ask two (up to three) people who know your academic and professional work; include your employer if you are employed.
Send them your draft development impact statement and course choices.

Ask for a signed PDF on institutional letterhead (or an email showing their official details) covering how long they have known you, your academic ability, strengths and weaknesses, and your development impact potential.
Set a deadline at least five days before yours, then upload the PDFs in CSC Central.
tips: References must be in the referee's own words — do not write them yourself.
avoid: Unsigned Word documents or letters on plain paper.
check: Two signed PDF references are uploaded.

steps.title: Complete every section and submit before 20 October
steps.why: Applications cannot be edited after submission and late ones are not accepted.
do: Paste final answers into each section of CSC Central.
Check your three course preferences and their order.
Upload passport/ID, transcripts and references; confirm each file opens.
Proofread names, dates and grades.
Submit before 16:00 UK time on the deadline and save the confirmation.
Nigeria: download and print the completed application PDF — FSB asks you to bring it to the interview.
tips: Submit two or three days early; the portal slows on deadline day.
avoid: Forgetting to select a nominating body.
check: I have a confirmation and a printed copy.

Watch: Commonwealth Scholarship 2027/28: How to Apply Step by Step – Application Form Guide (Gift Ifunanya)

steps.title: Prepare for the nominator's screening and interview
steps.why: Your nominating body decides whether you are sent to the CSC. FSB assesses academic merit, development impact and study plan.
do: Watch your email and the Federal Ministry of Education / FSB channels for interview dates.
Bring your printed application, original certificates, NYSC certificate and ID.
Practise a two-minute summary of your development problem, course and plan.
Prepare answers on why the UK, why this course, and how you will measure impact.
tips: Contact FSB at fsb@education.gov.ng if you hear nothing and dates are near.
check: I can explain my plan in two minutes without notes.

steps.title: Results, offer and pre-departure
steps.why: Results come by email around July 2027. Offers are withdrawn if you do not respond in time.
do: Check email (including spam) from spring 2027.
Reply to any CSC email within the time given.
Get an unconditional offer from your placed university.
Apply for your UK student visa and follow the CSC handbook for travel and stipend.
tips: Read the CSC handbook before you travel — it explains allowances and rules.
avoid: Planning to switch to a Graduate visa — Commonwealth Scholars must return home.
check: I know my next step after the result.

faq.a: Not for the CSC. Your university may still ask for English evidence.
No fee for the CSC. Universities may charge their own fees.
Not for the Master's award. The PhD award accepts a 2:2 plus a relevant master's.

faq.q: Do I have to apply through FSB if I am Nigerian?
faq.a: Yes, through FSB or an eligible NGO nominator. The CSC does not accept direct applications.
The CSC states none. Check your nominator's advert.
Yes, and a child allowance may apply, but dependants' airfares are not funded.
